items.title: David Finck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 29, 2015
items.q: And actually there’s a very funny story because Cole Porter got upset with Frank changing some of the words and he sent Frank a letter

ctx.x: Yeah. [sings distorted notes]. And it’s amazing. And I sat there and I said just sing the song. Can’t you just sing the song? Otherwise write your own. Because it didn’t make it more emotional, it didn’t deliver anything more, it was just her being about her. And you know I get upset by this stuff because if it’s a song I really like and somebody does that I’m like oh God, why are you doing that. Frank Sinatra, in my opinion, probably one of the greatest musicians I could think of, had a way of making the song…

think it worked out okay, but I can tell you this. I saw Frank sing two or three times. At Carnegie Hall I jumped out of my seat like it was The Beatles when he walked out on stage I was like, “Wow.” It was exquisite. And then I heard him later at Radio City Music Hall and I was way in the back in the nosebleed seats, only ones I could afford, but he sang “One for my Baby” and it wasn’t even that I felt like he was singing to me. I felt like I was sitting at the bar next to him. Like that’s pretty amazing. Really…
